cat > src/main/resources/db/migration/V4__person_name_unique.sql <<'EOF'
-- A person's name is unique on its sheet, without regard to case. Names are stored trimmed, so the
-- key is the lower-cased name.
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN name_key VARCHAR(200) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (LOWER(name));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX person_sheet_name ON person (sheet_id, name_key);
EOF
cat > $P/CheckPersonName.java <<'EOF'
package net.officefloor.hq.app.person;

import net.officefloor.plugin.variable.Val;

/** Refuses a name already used by another person on the sheet (ignoring case; names are trimmed). */
public class CheckPersonName {
    public void check(@Val PersonRequest request, @Val Person person, PersonRepository repository)
            throws InvalidPersonException {
        boolean taken = repository.findBySheetIdOrderByIdAsc(person.getSheetId()).stream()
                .anyMatch((other) -> !other.getId().equals(person.getId())
                        && other.getName().equalsIgnoreCase(request.name()));
        if (taken) {
            throw new InvalidPersonException("The name " + request.name() + " is already in use on this sheet.");
        }
    }
}
EOF

content.text:
A person's name now has to be unique on the sheet, ignoring case and any spaces before or after it, and the acceptance test passes with `bin/e2e`.

Names were already trimmed before being stored, so that part needed no change. What I added:

- **Server:** a new `CheckPersonName` step runs before the save when adding a person (`people.POST.yml`) and before the change is applied when editing one (`{personId}.PUT.yml`). It refuses the request if another person on the sheet already has the name, ignoring case; the edited person's own current name doesn't count as a clash. A refusal comes back as a 400 error, and nothing is written to the store.
- **Database:** a migration, `V4__person_name_unique.sql`, adds a lower-cased copy of the name, calculated by the database, and a unique index on sheet plus that name. This also catches two users saving the same name at the same moment. That race isn't tested, and the losing request would come back as an unhandled server error rather than the 400, though the form still shows its error message.
- **Form:** when a save is refused, the error message now says "a name is required and must not already be in use." It's a fixed message: the screen doesn't show the server's more specific reason.

The database is in-memory and rebuilt on every start, so existing duplicate names can't break the new unique index.
